entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Ivan Ivanovich Sollertinsky was a Soviet polymath. He specialized in fields including linguistics, theatre, literature, history, and philology, but was most known for his work in the musical field as a critic and musicologist. He was a professor at the Leningrad Conservatory, as well as an artistic director of the Leningrad Philharmonic, and a prominent orator. In these capacities, he was an active promoter of Mahler's music in the Soviet Union. Sollertinsky was also interested in ballet and often wrote essays on the subject during the 1930s, along with teaching ballet history at the Leningrad Choreographic Institute.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Sollertinsky's promotion of Mahler's music in the Soviet Union had a significant impact on the country's musical landscape, introducing his works to a new generation of composers and musicians. His work as an artistic director of the Leningrad Philharmonic also helped shape the orchestra's repertoire.
